promise: Turn an action boundary into a testable constraint harness, with legal actions still possible.
audience: People building agent tools, action validators and bounded environments.
trigger: Design, repair or evaluate constraints on agent actions.

modes.name: Explore
modes.output: An action/state model and explicit feasibility limits.

modes.name: Build
modes.output: A spec, validator and tests for legal and illegal actions.

modes.name: Debug
modes.when: A harness blocks valid work or leaks illegal actions.
modes.output: A focused failure diagnosis and measured refinement.

examples.title: Keep a file reader inside its root
examples.brief: Use Constraint Builder to specify a file-reading tool that may read project files but may not escape its root. Show legal reads, traversal attempts, symlink cases and false rejections before proposing a checker. Do not execute the proposed actions.
examples.before: A broad deny rule blocks every file operation.
examples.after: A boundary specification and traversal/symlink cases distinguish allowed reads from escaped paths.
examples.why: A measured false-rejection check preserves useful actions while testing the boundary.

boundaries: A skill alone does not enforce a sandbox or establish legal compliance.

verification.name: Functional acceptance
verification.expected: Supplied fictional tasks exercise actual mechanisms and failure boundaries.
verification.evidence: 72 native gate/scaffold checks passed; provider-backed loop needs optional litellm and was not accepted.

verification.name: Native host acceptance
verification.expected: Actual provider/host/desktop/daemon/runner acceptance for the selected adapter.
verification.evidence: No live model, real desktop transaction, invitation, deployment or production data migration was performed by this functional baseline.

sources.role: Primary retained owner history, mechanisms and records; portable method consolidates the listed entry points.

consolidation: One portable method entry with mode references; original native engines, agents and records retained as optional adapters.
publication_status: Installation and evidence scopes are documented below.

marketing.headline: Give your agent a boundary it can actually test.
marketing.lead: For developers building agent tools. Turn “the agent may do this, but never that” into an action specification, a checker and examples that show whether useful work is still possible.

benefits.title: Catch an escaped action
benefits.body: Put the check at the dispatch boundary, where an action can be accepted or refused.

benefits.title: Keep valid work possible
benefits.body: Test allowed actions alongside forbidden ones, so a boundary does not win by blocking everything.

benefits.title: Know what remains untested
benefits.body: Keep unseen cases, enforcement limits and the next acceptance test visible.

walkthrough.title: Describe the boundary
walkthrough.detail: Name the real state, allowed actions, irreversible costs and anything a checker cannot decide.

walkthrough.title: Build the smallest checker
walkthrough.detail: Write legal and illegal examples before tuning a validator. Start with a local gate before adding an optional engine.

walkthrough.title: Challenge both sides
walkthrough.detail: Test escapes and false rejections, then keep the measured result and the unresolved cases.

use_when: You are adding an agent action that needs a testable boundary.
A guard blocks legitimate work or allows a forbidden action.
You need a held-out test set before refining a constraint.
not_for: A substitute for a real sandbox, dispatch integration or a legal review.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Constraint Builder to specify a file-reading tool that may read project files but may not escape its root. Show legal reads, traversal attempts, symlink cases and false rejections before proposing a checker. Do not execute the proposed actions.
marketing.output_preview:
Boundary: reads stay inside the selected project root

Action                         Expected    Reason
read docs/guide.md             allow       ordinary project read
read ../outside.txt           refuse      escapes the root
read linked-secret.txt        refuse      resolved target is outside
read missing.txt              error       not an access-policy violation

Next gate: exercise the checker at the real dispatch boundary.
marketing.example_note: Fictional file-tool design. These are expected cases for a proposed checker, not a claim of sandbox enforcement.
install_notes: Python 3.11 or later is required by the portable install/build helper. The installed method runs through your agent host.
The portable skill and local checker use Python 3. No model key is needed to install or inspect them.
The checker evaluates trusted candidate Python locally; it is not an isolation boundary for hostile code.
The original Pico, Nano, Micro and provider-backed refinement engines are optional.
marketing.proof_summary: Local gate and scaffold tests exercise legal actions, illegal actions and failure paths. The provider-backed refinement loop and deployment into a real dispatch boundary require separate acceptance.
marketing.next_step: Start with one action boundary and an explicit list of cases the checker must distinguish.

name: amplifier-capability-constraint-builder
version_basis: No project version recorded; version remains null. The shared portable installer selects source with an explicit full Git commit; legacy and native routes follow their own documentation.

portable_method.name: constraint-builder
portable_method.contract: Agent Skills directory; caller applies the method; no independent execution loop is installed.

portable.input: Caller task and explicitly authorized context
portable.output: Turn an action boundary into a testable constraint harness, with legal actions still possible.
portable.failure: Report insufficient evidence, unsupported context or host limitation; never turn discovery into an execution claim.

native.status: Existing declared entrypoints preserved; runtime signatures, service access and installation tests remain separate evidence.

installation.scope: Shared canonical portable installer only; not the legacy repository helper or native package installation.

runtime.status: Host/caller authorizes each operation; installation is not a tool allowlist or standing approval.
declared_boundaries: A skill alone does not enforce a sandbox or establish legal compliance.

secret_names.native_runtime_inventory: See native documentation; no credentials are bundled or inferred.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: The goose at the gate.
film.blurb: In 71 seconds, a guard goose honks at every request: nothing escapes, and nothing gets done. Constraint Builder starts with cases before any checker: a plain read is allowed, a path that climbs out is refused, a link that looks local but leads outside is refused, and a missing file is an error, not an attack. The checker counts both mistakes, blocked work and escapes. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The file tool, the cases and the results are a fictional example. Passing supplied cases does not prove unseen safety; the film shows how the skill behaves and reports no results.

shared_portable.applies_when: portable_method is declared; otherwise describe native interfaces without executing installation
guarantees: Tracked portable source membership and source-byte checks

legacy_repository.documentation: Existing install_commands and repository installation documentation, where provided.
legacy_repository.source_policy: Operator-controlled current working-tree copy. It can include untracked files and can operate outside a Git checkout; no uniform Git pin or SHA-256 transaction receipt is enforced.
legacy_repository.permissions: Review the specific command and destination; shared-installer transaction and permission guarantees do not describe this route.

native.documentation: interfaces.native, runtime_install_commands and project installation documentation, where provided.
native.source_policy: Native packaging, host composition and download routes retain their own version and provenance rules; shared portable receipt guarantees do not automatically apply.
native.permissions: Package builds may execute build tools; dependency or artifact downloads may use the network. Review the documented command, dependencies, destination and runtime authorization separately.
